previous_content: ## Routing
An explicit `--commit` loads [`references/commit-evidence.md`](references/commit-evidence.md) and stops ordinary Capture and
implementation routing. It needs Git repositories, not a Tarav Project.
`--design --dialogue --wiki` loads [`references/design-dialogue.md`](references/design-dialogue.md) and captures the
conversation as a dialogue. Select this route before implementation routing.
It does not create an Impl.Req or select an implementation phase.
Implementation phases live in
[`references/impl/phases.md`](references/impl/phases.md) and read context from
a context backend; the Project.Wiki is the only active one. The Model backend
is parked: `--model` and legacy notes carrying Impl.Req.Diagram require
clarification before any mutation; never silently migrate a request.
Do not reread a skill `references/` file that was already read completely and
remains available in context. Reread it only if it changed, its contents were
lost or materially reduced through compaction, or a specific uncertainty
requires it.
`--impact` selects input: the implementation delta implied by recent in-chat
design, optionally narrowed by FOCUS. It does not select an implementation
phase. Without an implementation selector, `--design --impact` follows
{{skw:link-0}} and reports only.
With `--impl` or an explicit implementation selector such as `--dev`, route
through [`references/impl.md`](references/impl.md), which uses the same
assessment before running the selected workflow. Thus `--impl --design
--impact` is implementation Design, not the read-only report route.
Bare `--design` does not select Design Impact. Standalone Design Impact does
not compose with Capture; implementation routes retain their ordinary capture
contract.
`--ground`, optionally qualified by `--notebook`, loads and follows
[`references/ground.md`](references/ground.md). It is read-only and does not
compose with Capture or implementation. Infer the Project from the task and cwd.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 2c482dc7754e -->
`--explain-me` loads and follows [`references/explain-me.md`](references/explain-me.md).
Explain Me is read-only and does not compose with Capture or implementation.
Ordinary Capture routes load and follow [`references/capture.md`](references/capture.md).
`--capture --wiki`, including its `--target` and `--audit` routes, instead
loads and follows [`references/wiki-capture.md`](references/wiki-capture.md).
It edits Project.Wiki Markdown only in the ordinary non-audit route and never
enters Diagram Model capture.
`--capture --inline`, including its `--audit` route, loads and follows
[`references/inline-capture.md`](references/inline-capture.md).
Reading Club routes load and follow
[`references/reading-club.md`](references/reading-club.md).
Issue routes first load [`references/issues.md`](references/issues.md), which
selects one Issue workflow without creating a separate Parking.Note object.
Implementation routes first load
[`references/impl.md`](references/impl.md), which selects exactly one
implementation workflow module. Without an explicit route, infer capture,
Issue, or implementation only when the conversational request is clear.
The runtime commands `::discuss`, `::review`, `::approve <token>`, `::land`,
and `::land-all-approved` belong to the running Capture workflow. Reading
navigation commands such as `::forward`, `::backward`, `::capture`, and
`::annotate`, together with reading commands such as `::narrate`, belong to a
running Reading Club workflow. They are not initial Batchy.Skill calls.

content: ## Assessment
Read the relevant project instructions, then inspect the current code,
documentation, and skills affected by the design. Follow actual producers,
consumers, and retained-data contracts where needed to establish impact.
Distinguish implemented behavior from documentation, examples, and future intent.
Compare the design with that evidence and report:
- what already aligns and needs no change;
- concrete changes needed, with affected surfaces and their reason;
- unresolved design decisions or unavailable evidence that prevent a conclusion.
Include data migration or consumer consequences when a proposed change affects
them. A development principle may call for guidance or better examples rather
than runtime enforcement. Do not invent mechanics merely to make every design
statement executable, and do not treat a lack of evidence as proof of a gap.
Keep the result concise and in chat. Link the inspected surfaces that support
the conclusions, state the scope of the inspection, and distinguish necessary
changes from optional improvements. It is valid to conclude that no
implementation action is needed.

      "content": [
        "## Landing Through Tarav.Diagram",
        "",
        "Create no `Diagram.Draft` or `Capture.Manifest` during ordinary reviewed",
        "discussion. After `::land` or `::land-all-approved`, materialize a short-lived",
        "Draft from the settled proposal, check it, and apply it. In automatic mode,",

        "bounded batch is settled; the initial invocation already authorizes landing.",
        "",
        "`Capture.Manifest` is the Draft apply operation's internal transport format,",
        "not a second writable workspace. A workflow such as `--impl` may instead keep",
        "a durable Draft when reconciliation across several slices is useful.",
        "",
        "The Manifest is a faithful mechanical compilation. Entity creation and",
        "semantic evolution go in `ships`; claims about existing entities or editions",
        "go in `annotations`:",
        "",
        "- each semantic Line is a `Diagram.Line.Ship` draft whose edition retains its",
        "  exact wording, full `line_type`, producer Chatlas Turn, and rooted User",
        "  support; the Ship record retains its Model and Block references;",
        "- reviewed Lines retain `Verbatim.Gate` data containing the shared opaque",
        "  token and exact proposal and approval Turn references;",
        "- automatic Lines omit Gates;",
        "- one approval exchange may cover several exact Lines when the proposal turn",
        "  contains every wording, but each Line retains its own Gate instance;",
        "- each new Block is a `Diagram.Block.Ship` whose first edition retains its full",
        "  `block_type`; its Block.Type determines the allowed Line.Type vocabulary;",
        "- append a fresh edition UUID to an existing Ship when the approved material",
        "  continues that entity; allocate a new Ship UUID when it creates a new one;",
        "- Annotations may add review, type, tag, rename-transition, or other claims,",
        "  but they never create the Ship they discuss;",
        "- a `Line.Annotation` is a free-standing natural-language Line whose ordered",
        "  editions use an explicit `arguments` context instead of a containing Block;",
        "- use only `Line.Annotation` for open relational capture until a more",
        "  specialized Annotation.Type is independently designed and justified;",
        "- missing, unknown, conflicting, or disallowed Object.Types are writable POIs,",
        "  not permission to silently substitute another Type.",

        "only the new editions of an existing Ship:",

        "{",
        "  \"class\": \"Tarav.Diagram.Capture.Manifest\",",
        "  \"schema_version\": 2,",
        "  \"model_ship\": \"<model-ship-uuid>\",",
        "  \"ships\": [",
        "    {",
        "      \"id\": \"<block-ship-uuid>\",",
        "      \"type\": \"Diagram.Block.Ship\",",
        "      \"model_ship\": \"<model-ship-uuid>\",",
        "      \"editions\": [",
        "        {",
        "          \"id\": \"<block-edition-uuid>\",",
        "          \"block_type\": \"Design.Block\",",
        "          \"data\": {\"label\": \"<block-label>\"}",
        "        }",
        "      ]",
        "    },",

        "      \"type\": \"Diagram.Line.Ship\",",
        "      \"model_ship\": \"<model-ship-uuid>\",",
        "      \"block_ship\": \"<block-ship-uuid>\",",
        "      \"editions\": [",

        "          \"line_type\": \"Design.Line.Principle\",",
        "          \"producer\": {\"session_identity\": \"...\", \"turn_address\": \"...\", \"turn_hash\": \"...\"},",
        "          \"support\": [{\"root\": {\"session_identity\": \"...\", \"turn_address\": \"...\", \"turn_hash\": \"...\"}, \"neighborhood\": []}],",
        "          \"data\": {\"text\": \"<exact approved wording>\"}",
        "        }",
        "      ]",
        "    }",
        "  ],",
        "  \"annotations\": []",
        "}",
        "```",
        "",
        "A free-standing Line connecting existing objects compiles under",
        "`annotations`. Reusing its Annotation UUID appends another claim edition:",
        "",
        "```json",
        "{",
        "  \"id\": \"<line-annotation-uuid>\",",

        "    }",

      "content": [
        "## Capture workflow",
        "",
        "1. Read the selected project's instructions and resolve its Project.Wiki.",
        "2. Resolve and refresh the current chat exactly once through",
        "   `tarav-chatlas-my-session-id`. Reuse its provider, native session ID, and",

        "3. Select the minimum sufficient User Turns from the requested focus and",

        "   hashes are not already known.",
        "4. Read the current daily Note when present and inspect the wiki to resolve any",
        "   useful topical placement as described above.",
        "5. Draft the mandatory daily narrative of what relevantly happened.",
        "6. Draft topical integration when useful, using the explicit target when one",
        "   was supplied. Decide section editing or edition splitting from the",
        "   discussion's actual semantics.",
        "7. Resolve selected Turn groups through Chatlas Query and render provisional",
        "   references with `Inlined.Capture.Markdown.Reference.Renderer`.",
        "8. Add or reuse session declarations and attach provisional references",
        "   directly to the blocks they ground.",
        "9. For every changed Note containing provisional markers, run",
        "   `tarav breadcrumbs submit chatlas-context --surface <NOTE> --json` exactly",
        "   once after the Note content is final.",
        "10. Re-read every changed Note and run `tarav breadcrumbs audit",
        "    chatlas-context --surface <NOTE> --json`; inspect semantic placement after",
        "    its mechanical checks.",
        "11. Inspect the scoped diff and commit the complete Project.Wiki under",
        "   the Git-closure rules above.",
        "12. Report the daily and topical destinations, sections added or amended,",
        "    Breadcrumb IDs, commit identity, and unresolved POIs.",
        "",
        "If a topic placement remains genuinely ambiguous, complete the daily capture",
        "and report that no topical integration was made. Capture must not fail merely",
        "because the wiki can be organized better later.",

        "If submission cannot register, typically because a sandbox prevents writing",
        "to the Tarav data folder, leave the read-only trace. Keep the provisional",
        "`tarav.context` markers where they are and keep their session resolvable.",
        "Do not remove the markers or invent Breadcrumb labels, and report the",
        "registration as pending, not as done. A later session that can write runs the",
        "same `submit` and `audit` commands on the surface; nothing has to be guessed",
        "while the declaration is intact.",
        "",
        "A session first used by a later section may be declared in a",
        "`tarav.sessions` block beside that section, so earlier Breadcrumb lines do",

        "",

        "",
        "### `Reading.Source.Frame`",
        "",
        "A `Reading.Source.Frame` is the bounded in-chat window through which source",
        "content is presented:",
        "",

        "   marker explicitly signals essentially verbatim source wording, allowing",
        "   only non-semantic typography or client-presentation adaptations. Never use",
        "   it for Agent paraphrase.",
        "2. Preserve source order.",
        "3. Do not insert paraphrases, summaries, explanations, or connective prose",
        "   inside the Frame.",
        "4. Mark omissions explicitly with `[…]`.",

        "   must not change. When adapted substantially from source notation, present",
        "   them as separate terminal-friendly blocks rather than implying textual",
        "   verbatim fidelity with `>`.",

        "   explicitly.",
        "7. Keep the chunk ID and location outside the quoted source content.",
        "8. Keep interpretation outside the Frame, normally in discussion or a",
        "   `Reading.Narration.Frame`.",
        "9. Select a coherent, reasonably sized reading unit.",
        "",

        "what matters, incorporates relevant prior discussion and User concerns,",

        "the developing interpretation. It is non-mutating and non-navigating. Keep it",
        "shorter than the current Source Frame when practical and never longer than",

        "## Chat presentation",
        "",
        "Treat chat as a flexible reading interface over the project transcript. Keep",
        "source prose identifiable: reproduce it faithfully when quoting, and label",
        "paraphrases or summaries. Chat presentation may otherwise adapt formatting for",
        "the active client and does not need to preserve the transcript's syntax.",
        "",
        "When the client does not render LaTeX, a `Reading.Source.Frame` may present",
        "equations in a terminal-friendly Unicode or plain-text form. For example,",
        "present `\\beta_G^{\\mathrm{c}}(\\beta_O)` as `βG,critical(βO)`. Do not add a",
        "verbal explanation inside the Source Frame unless that explanation is itself",
        "source prose. The chat does not need to repeat the original LaTeX because it",
        "remains available in the project transcript. If an expression cannot be",
        "simplified safely, retain its source notation rather than guessing; explain",
        "its structure or role later in discussion or a `Reading.Narration.Frame`.",
        "Never silently change the mathematical relation.",
        "",
        "### Growing terminal-presentation examples",
        "",
        "This list is the skill's explicit place for accumulating useful presentation",
        "examples discovered during real reading sessions. When a new recurring",
        "notation is rendered successfully, append a compact source → chat example",
        "here. Prefer additions that generalize beyond one paper; do not turn isolated",
        "expressions into mandatory syntax.",
        "",
        "Current examples:",
        "",
        "- labels and indices: `u_L^{(i)}` → `uL[i]`;",
        "- critical or descriptive qualifiers: `\\beta_G^{\\mathrm{c}}` →",
        "  `βG,critical`;",
        "- averages: `\\langle u_L\\rangle` → `⟨uL⟩` or `mean(uL)`;",
        "- fractions: `\\frac{x}{y}` → `x / y`;",
        "- sums: `\\sum_{i=1}^{N}u_i` → `Σ[i=1…N] u[i]`;",
        "- derivatives: `\\frac{d\\langle u_L\\rangle}{d\\beta_G}` →",
        "  `d⟨uL⟩ / dβG`;",
        "- bounds and constraints: `0\\leq u_G\\leq U_G` → `0 ≤ uG ≤ UG`;",
        "- powers and roots: `x^2` → `x²`, while general powers remain `x^n`, and",
        "  `\\sqrt{x}` → `sqrt(x)`;",
        "- piecewise expressions or equation systems: use one aligned plain-text line",
        "  per case or relation, with short labels where needed.",
        "",
        "These are examples, not a mechanical conversion standard. Choose notation",
        "that is readable and consistent within the current discussion.",

        "",
        "- `::forward` — run an automatic annotation checkpoint over pending",

        "  redefining progress.",

        "  `Reading.Source.Frame`; wait when the destination is ambiguous.",
        "- `::capture` and `::annotate` — exact aliases: review discussion since the",
        "  previous checkpoint, preserve valuable User-Touched material in the project",
        "  transcript or notes, remain on the current chunk, and produce a compact",
        "  `Reading.Capture.Report`.",
        "- `::stop` — capture useful pending discussion and preserve the current",
        "  position for later resumption.",
        "- `::reprint` — reproduce the current `Reading.Source.Frame` without moving.",
        "- `::narrate` — produce a `Reading.Narration.Frame` for the current chunk.",
        "- `::help` — explain this workflow and its commands as `Reading.Help`.",
        "- `::status` — report the active project, current location, approximate",
        "  progress, and uncaptured discussion as a compact `Reading.Status.Report`.",
        "- `::reload` — reread the project transcript and notes, reconcile the",
        "  disposable session, and do not advance. Produce a compact reconciliation",
        "  report, followed by the current `Reading.Source.Frame` when useful.",
        "",
        "Ordinary User messages keep the current chunk active. If a command cannot be",
        "fulfilled exactly after transcript changes, explain the recovery and re-anchor",
        "visibly before continuing.",

        "## Capture",
        "",
        "Capture is selective and Agent-operated. Preserve the User's corrections,",
        "recollections, questions, and settled interpretations close to the relevant",
        "text or in project notes. Use ordinary Tarav capture primitives and the",
        "Chatlas-context Breadcrumb workflow where a User Turn materially contextualizes",
        "retained Markdown; do not invent a Reading Club specific annotation system.",
        "A checkpoint does not require turning every message into prose: the Agent may",
        "add a settled interpretation, preserve an",
        "open question, correct the transcript, add only a contextual reference, or",
        "report that nothing new required durable capture. For each changed file with",
        "provisional `tarav.context` markers, run",
        "`tarav breadcrumbs submit chatlas-context --surface <FILE> --json` once after",
        "its content is final, then run `tarav breadcrumbs audit chatlas-context",
        "--surface <FILE> --json`.",
        "",
        "If submission cannot register, typically because a sandbox prevents writing",
        "to the Tarav data folder, leave the read-only trace. Keep the provisional",
        "`tarav.context` markers where they are and keep their session resolvable.",
        "Do not remove the markers or invent Breadcrumb labels, and report the",
        "registration as pending, not as done. A later session that can write runs the",
        "same `submit` and `audit` commands on the surface; nothing has to be guessed",

        "After `::capture` or `::annotate`, report compactly what was preserved and do",
        "not move. Never advance as a side effect of capture unless the User sent",
        "`::forward`. At `::stop`, report the retained project and approximate position",
        "compactly.",
        "",
        "`::forward` is a compound command: it may briefly report what its annotation",
        "checkpoint preserved, but its principal visible output is always the new",
        "`Reading.Source.Frame`."

        "```",
        "",

        "# Git Commit Evidence",
        "",
        "Use this module for `tarav-hugentics --commit [PATH...]` and for Git commits",
        "owned by modifying Hugentics workflows. Read-only routes never commit.",
        "Multi-repository work commits each repository independently.",
        "",
        "## Routes",
        "",
        "The standalone `--commit` invocation authorizes one completion commit in each",
        "selected repository. It creates no artificial start checkpoint. Explicit paths",
        "select their owning repositories and exact worktree scope. Without paths, commit",
        "all current changes in repositories already established by the active task; when",
        "there is no such task scope, use the current Git repository. Do not recursively",
        "discover or absorb unrelated repositories.",
        "",
        "A modifying Hugentics workflow instead commits often in every repository it",
        "mutates: a start checkpoint before its first edit, a commit after every",
        "verified slice, and a completion commit. The initial invocation authorizes all",
        "of them, including the external work they absorb under the rules below.",
        "",
        "## Scope",
        "",
        "The agent declares the exact repository-relative paths it is committing. The",
        "workflow's own commits include only files it changed.",
        "",
        "External work is any uncommitted change the workflow did not make, whoever",
        "made it. Frequent commits matter more than its provenance:",
        "",
        "- **Start checkpoint.** Before the first edit, always make one in every",
        "  repository the workflow will mutate. Commit every pre-existing change, inside",
        "  or outside the work scope, including the workflow's own live note; when the",
        "  repository is clean, make an empty commit. A clean tree, a tree holding only",
        "  the note, or a commit made earlier in the session is never a reason to skip.",
        "- **Stale external work.** At every slice boundary, when the repository holds",
        "  external work and its last commit is at least one hour old, commit that",
        "  external work.",
        "- **Slice commit.** After a slice's checks pass and its capture ran, commit the",
        "  files the slice changed.",
        "- **Completion.** Commit the remaining files the workflow changed.",
        "",
        "Commit external work as found, in its own commit apart from the workflow's",
        "files, with the `unknown-session` gap marker unless its discussion is",
        "identifiable. A file holding both external and own changes goes into the",
        "workflow's commit, and the workflow's log says so. Committing another",
        "session's work loses nothing: the commit is a snapshot, and later edits remain",
        "ordinary changes.",
        "",
        "Skip a commit only when the Git state prevents it: a merge or rebase in",
        "progress, unresolved conflicts, or an index lock that persists after retries.",
        "Record `skip: <reason>` in the workflow's log. Another agent's changes are",
        "never a reason to skip.",
        "",
        "## Manifest and message",
        "",
        "Write a temporary JSON manifest with this shape:",
        "",
        "```json",
        "{",
        "  \"type\": \"Tarav.Git.CommitEvidence.Manifest\",",
        "  \"repository\": \"/absolute/repository\",",
        "  \"files\": [\"relative/path.py\"],",
        "  \"message\": \"Subject\\n\\n- relative/path.py: bounded change\\n<!-- tarav.context <alias>:<turn-prefix> -->\",",
        "  \"allow_empty\": false",
        "}",
        "```",
        "",
        "Declare sessions in the message with the ordinary `tarav.sessions` block.",
        "Each human-readable `- ` change group ends with one or more provisional",
        "`tarav.context` markers, or with exactly one honest gap marker:",
        "",
        "```text",
        "<!-- tarav.evidence agent-initiated -->",
        "<!-- tarav.evidence unknown-session -->",
        "```",
        "",
        "Use `agent-initiated` when the committing agent decided the change without a",
        "supporting User Turn. Use `unknown-session` for pre-existing work whose",
        "discussion cannot be identified. Evidence is best effort; do not fabricate",
        "coverage. Tarav creates Breadcrumb IDs and the recoverable evidence envelope.",
        "Do not author either one manually in a new manifest.",
        "",
        "## Commit and recovery",
        "",
        "Run:",
        "",
        "```bash",
        "tarav git commit --manifest <manifest.json> --json",

        "",
        "Tarav validates and registers Breadcrumb evidence, commits only the declared",

## Preamble

This document is the Constitution of Tarav.

It states the fundamental principles and boundaries of the Tarav system. Any surface claiming to be part of Tarav must comply with this Constitution.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb c3bd772ca1ca -->

The Constitution is intentionally general, incomplete, and amendable. It does not contain all Tarav design truth or require a single implementation.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb ecd16660e190 -->

When a Tarav design conflicts with the Constitution, the conflict must be surfaced. It can be resolved by changing the design, amending the Constitution, or changing both.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 1c3656d59617 -->

## Purpose

Tarav is an external `Agents.Harness` intended to enhance collaboration between Users and Agents. It provides tools and workflows addressing recurring problems in that collaboration.

Concretely, Tarav is an extensible Python library. Its capabilities can be integrated into a wider system and composed into specialized harnesses for particular Projects.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 529226730418 -->

Capture, including recording `User.Touched.Data`, annotation primitives, contextualization, checks, and workflow coordination are concrete capabilities through which Tarav supports collaboration. They can evolve while remaining consistent with this purpose.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 3d347443ec3e -->
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb f8a6d1c8c52c -->


## Projects

A `Project` is a fundamental Tarav concept. Tarav's capabilities can be selected, extended, and combined to build a harness for a particular Project.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 8178981fa771 -->

## Agent Harness Boundary

An Agent is a harness around an LLM. Tarav is an `Agents.Harness`: a harness around Agents that supports collaboration between those Agents and Users.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb e1afd7dc0934 -->

Tarav may provide mechanisms for launching or operating Agents, but agent execution is not its defining responsibility.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 7353b15ca16e -->

Tarav supports the contextualization of agent reasoning; it does not prescribe the internal reasoning of an Agent.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb e0644e75d73d -->

## Mechanical and Agentic Work

Tarav must use deliberately simple, bounded code to perform work that can be specified reliably and to provide data, context, and signals to flexible Agents.

Tarav should mechanize as much of the common case as practical without encoding complex or brittle solutions merely to avoid Agent involvement.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 193b02b6c8d2 -->

Ambiguous, interpretive, open-ended, and long-tail work should be routed to Agents.

Agent fallback is an intended part of Tarav architecture, not a failure of mechanical automation.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 49fa142669d1 -->

## User Context

Tarav is biased toward enriching agent context with `User.Touched.Data`. It must help agents work as fully contextualized on the user as possible.

This grounding does not claim that `User.Touched.Data` is authoritative or correct. Tarav does not prescribe how an agent reasons from that context.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb e638ee17754d -->

## Natural Workflows and Extensibility

Tarav must fit `User.Natural.Workflows` rather than require users to adopt one prescribed Tarav workflow.

Tarav must be flexible and designed for extension so users, agents, and implementations can adapt it to their natural collaboration patterns.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb c0c3c12db0f2 -->

Extensions may introduce different mechanisms and workflows, but any surface claiming to be part of Tarav remains bound by this Constitution.

## Session Goals

Tarav-supported user-agent sessions may pursue both the user’s immediate objective and the capture and enrichment of `User.Touched.Data`.

The user controls the foreground workflow. Tarav must not stop or redirect product development to require Diagram enrichment.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 177f4e2677c5 -->

When the user chooses development, the session develops. Enrichment may occur organically without obstructing that work. When the user chooses capture, curation, or enrichment, the session pursues that work directly.

Tarav must provide primitives that make collecting, annotating, and curating `User.Touched.Data` cheap and organic within `User.Natural.Workflows`.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb bfab21d025fb -->

Completeness measures may guide enrichment and surface opportunities, but they must not gate work or impose a globally complete Diagram.

## Mutation and Validation

Tarav must be evolvable and migration-friendly. Its code, schemas, and data are amendable. For product surfaces, committed Git history together with retained work conversations is sufficient change evidence by default. Additional documentation or tracking may be added when useful, but exhaustive change explanations must not become a prerequisite for evolution.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 823eddb6a42f -->
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb a1e213b405af -->

The nonblocking validation commitment for capturing user data is stated in Capture First below.

Users, agents, and other consumers are the primary mutators of Tarav state.

## Checks and Findings

Tarav must provide extensible checking capabilities that help users and agents assess a Project’s state and surface findings with enough context to act on them.

Specific workflows define what gets checked, when checks run, and how findings are represented. A finding does not itself dictate the response; users, agents, and other consumers decide how to interpret and act on it.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 69c072923d44 -->

## Capture First

Tarav prioritizes recording `User.Touched.Data`. When data may contain or preserve `User.Touched.Data`, capture must occur before concerns about completeness, formatting, annotation quality, or other POIs are resolved.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 88630183a7af -->

Tarav capture must favor recoverable overcapture over irrecoverable failure to record touched data.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 627d3007ee2b -->

Validation must not block the capture of user data. Tarav considers this data highly valuable. When a capture path fails, the system must provide a simpler fallback, including retaining raw data for later processing. Capture comes first; validation and organization can follow.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 45e1f418f101 -->
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 96e54d858b65 -->

Once data enters Tarav, it may be curated, annotated, amended, enriched, and scored over time.

Tarav is not a general repository for Agent-generated summaries or content. Agent-generated data is not archived merely because it was generated; it may be archived when touched, deliberately selected, or captured as a safety margin against losing touched data.

## Logistical Extensions

Tarav must support integration with databases, query systems, and other logistical extensions that improve performance and access over Tarav data.

Tarav data remains authoritative. Logistical extensions may index, cache, query, or project that data, but they do not displace its authority.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 287596d1a3ec -->

## Collaboration Loop

Tarav is organized around a continuous collaboration loop:

```text
user-agent collaboration
          ↓ captures
       Touched.Data
          ↓ recorded by
      Tarav.Archive
          ↓ structured by
      Tarav.Diagram
          ↓ selected through
     Contextualization
          ↓ enriches
  user-agent collaboration
```

## Tarav.Archive

The main responsibility of `Tarav.Archive` is to record `User.Touched.Data`.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb a8662815421f -->

`Tarav.Archive` registers `Archive.Artifact`s and retains `Archive.Record`s about them.

An `Archive.Artifact` is the actual data identified by the Archive. An Artifact may be retained by the Archive, located elsewhere, or temporarily unavailable.

An `Archive.Record` is retained data associated with one Artifact. Records may preserve Archive bureaucracy, identity information, current and historical locations, observations, descriptions, fingerprints, and other hints about that Artifact.

`Tarav.Archive` records Artifacts and Records without regard to their origin, purpose, or meaning. Tarav must use the Archive to record `User.Touched.Data`; the Archive itself does not recognize or distinguish that data from anything else it records.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 73beb42996d3 -->

The Archive does not interpret the internal semantic structure of Artifacts. Consumers construct organization and meaning from Archive Artifacts and Records.

Archive Records do not need to agree. The Archive preserves attributed claims and observations without endorsing their correctness or meaning.

Archive Artifacts are immutable signal. A changed Artifact is another Artifact. Archive Records describing an Artifact are amendable: locations, annotations, fingerprints, and other information may evolve while the Record continues to describe the same Artifact.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 843ff542a6db -->
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 1278026470b5 -->

The Archive provides typed references whose contracts consumers must be able to inspect. A reference to an amendable Record follows its declared contract. The Archive must never silently provide a different Artifact in place of the identified Artifact. If it offers a substitute or another representation, it must make the substitution and its relationship to the requested Artifact explicit.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 461b2a55511f -->
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb cd281677c0ea -->

The Archive must help consumers locate Artifacts. When an Artifact is unavailable, the Archive must expose its retained location history, fingerprints, External Descriptors, and other available hints.

Archive Record coverage may be progressive and demand-driven. Tarav must permit Records to be enriched over time and must not require complete Record coverage as a precondition for capture, reference, or use.

Archive Records must favor representations cheap enough to retain broadly. Records have greater retention priority than the Artifacts they describe. When preservation tradeoffs are unavoidable, the Archive should discard an Artifact before its associated Records, while strongly prioritizing preservation of `User.Touched.Data`.

Consumers may register Artifacts as `External.Descriptors` of other Artifacts. An External Descriptors Record contains attributed references to other Artifacts declared to be useful descriptions, representations, or recovery hints for its target Artifact.

The Archive preserves External Descriptor references without endorsing their correctness or meaning. Each External Descriptor remains an ordinary Artifact with its own identity, locations, Records, and possible External Descriptors.

The Archive does not provide a general semantic relationship graph. Relationships beyond its bounded External Descriptor references, and the assessment of those relationships, belong to consumers such as `Tarav.Diagram`.

`Tarav.Archive` makes no commitment to downstream readers about Record formatting or which context a Record contains. Its responsibility is preservation, not presentation; readers are responsible for interpreting what it preserves.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 779ab9387f69 -->

## Tarav.Diagram

Tarav must provide an extensible Diagram capability for users and agents to express, navigate, and query semantic relationships. The Diagram is a place where users and agents can write ideas, observations, hypotheses, plans, and relationships, including relationships between runtime objects.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 1ab6e69980db -->

Workflows may define specialized semantics and grounding requirements for the material they place there. Relationships about `User.Touched.Data` are one application of this capability. Inclusion in the Diagram does not itself imply truth, validation, or grounding in archived evidence; Archive links and Assertion scores are not universal requirements for Diagram content.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb ad5919d18657 -->

## Contextualization

Tarav must provide extensible tooling and systems for selecting and presenting `Tarav.Diagram` content to collaborative user-agent sessions.

Context may begin with compact Ship editions or Annotations, but Tarav must preserve a navigable path from each contextualized Record to its linked supporting data.

Agents and other consumers must be able to expand that path on demand and inspect progressively deeper supporting context.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb a6d682f872ea -->


## Reference Contracts

Tarav references are typed. Their Types declare the contract under which data is identified and resolved. Some contracts permit maintenance such as schema changes; others commit to exact bytes.

References must never silently deliver data that violates their declared contract. They must provide a way to check for changes relevant to that contract. Hashes and retained hints can support these checks.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 2c09edaf5ab9 -->
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 4b3b5219ff55 -->
